classification.difficultyReason: Define success and express the given probability and its complement as a two-value distribution.

content.prompt: Write each Bernoulli distribution as a piecewise function. Define the success condition.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Passing a test if the probability of a pass is $\frac{7}{9}$

answer.short:
Let $X=1$ for a pass and $X=0$ for a fail.
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}\frac{7}{9}&x=1\\\frac{2}{9}&x=0\end{cases}$$
answer.worked:
Let $X=1$ for a pass and $X=0$ for a fail.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=0)&=1-\frac{7}{9}\\&=\frac{2}{9}\end{aligned}$$
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}\frac{7}{9}&x=1\\\frac{2}{9}&x=0\end{cases}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: An arrow hitting a target with probability 84%

answer.short:
Let $X=1$ for a hit and $X=0$ for a miss.
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}0.84&x=1\\0.16&x=0\end{cases}$$
answer.worked:
Let $X=1$ for a hit and $X=0$ for a miss.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=0)&=1-0.84\\&=0.16\end{aligned}$$
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}0.84&x=1\\0.16&x=0\end{cases}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Getting a head when tossing a fair coin

answer.short:
Let $X=1$ for a head and $X=0$ for a tail.
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{2}&x=1\\\frac{1}{2}&x=0\end{cases}$$
answer.worked:
Let $X=1$ for a head and $X=0$ for a tail. For a fair coin, $P(X=1)=\frac{1}{2}$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=0)&=1-\frac{1}{2}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$$
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{2}&x=1\\\frac{1}{2}&x=0\end{cases}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Winning a raffle in which you hold one of the 150 tickets sold and one winning ticket is selected at random

answer.short:
Let $X=1$ for a win and $X=0$ for a loss.
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{150}&x=1\\\frac{149}{150}&x=0\end{cases}$$
answer.worked:
Let $X=1$ for a win and $X=0$ for a loss. One of the 150 equally likely tickets is yours, so $P(X=1)=\frac{1}{150}$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=0)&=1-\frac{1}{150}\\&=\frac{149}{150}\end{aligned}$$
$$P(X=x)=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{150}&x=1\\\frac{149}{150}&x=0\end{cases}$$
